title.narrative: CONT CAC065 (Y3): Central America: a movement of wills for dignity

description.narrative: The Jesuit Central American Provincial Commission of the Social Apostolate (CPAS) understands that working for dignified life and justice requires deep reflection and collective audacity and that the future of Central America is forged by all of us, in community, in a network. For this reason, we are invited to trust in new forms of relationships: taking care of ourselves and our Common Home; promoting leadership that overcomes individualism; encouraging a new democratic political culture, in which the dignity of all people is at the centre. Together with the diversity of voices and perspectives of women, youth, popular movements, indigenous and Afro-descendant peoples, people in forced mobility and other groups, CPAS seeks to build alternatives and raise hope in the face of this capitalist, patriarchal and racist system that violates the Central American peoples. In synthesis, five are the most complex problems of the Central American reality that we face: Fading democratic systems Concentrating, exclusionary and predatory economic model. Risks and complexities in the forced mobilisation of people. Growing human rights violations: gender equality as a priority Communication: new narratives and inspiring agendas The project aims to assist in the implementation of the Strategic Directions 2023-2027 set by the Jesuits through two objectives: i) To strengthen networking and articulation at local, national and regional levels of works and sectors of the Society of Jesus in the Central American region (inwards). ii) To contribute to the development of regional proposals as a realisation of the "Faith and Justice" option in harmony with the religious, social, political, economic and cultural commitment of the social dimension that Jesuit works must promote (outwards).
